user_report: User reports rebooting before playing all five files.

reboot_evidence.method: /tmp and /run are tmpfs and are recreated empty at boot; /tmp/messages is the syslog and begins at boot
reboot_evidence.syslog_first_line: Aug 27 06:56:52 MiSTer syslog.info syslogd started: BusyBox v1.33.1
reboot_evidence.mister_clock: UTC; agent local clock is America/Phoenix (UTC-7), so MiSTer 07:09 = local 00:09
reboot_evidence.conclusion: Linux booted once at 06:56:52 UTC (23:56:52 local) and remained up continuously across block 1 and block 2. Block 2 was preceded by a core reload at 07:09 UTC, not by a Linux reboot. A core reload reconfigures the FPGA but does not restart Linux and does not clear the page cache.

block1_boot_correlation: block 1 capture 1 was taken at 23:58:14 local = 06:58:14 UTC, 82 seconds after the verified boot, so block 1 capture 1 is a confirmed genuine cold-after-boot sample at 1,103,135 starved cycles.

arm_helper_log.covers: a single playback session; the file is rewritten per run
arm_helper_log.would_block_distribution: logged at powers of two; every logged instance carries submitted=0, and the highest logged is 128 against a total of 190, so all 190 would-block events occur before the first byte is submitted
arm_helper_log.post_startup_blocking: none - after read event 1 the helper never blocks again
arm_helper_log.finish: reason=eof download=1 submitted=15150646 reads=3699 would_block=190, child exit_code=0

findings: All five block 2 sessions are clean: zero cadence outliers, zero missed deadlines, 449 pictures, 448 swaps, 15,150,646 bytes accepted, error_flags 0, quiet terminal.
The device evidence does not support a reboot before block 2. Linux booted once at 06:56:52 UTC and stayed up through both blocks; only the core was reloaded at 07:09 UTC.
Block 2 therefore ran against a page cache already warmed by block 1's five reads of the same file, which is the strongest support so far for the read-latency mechanism.
Block 1 capture 1 is confirmed as a genuine cold-after-boot sample, captured 82 seconds after the verified boot, and it gapped with 1,103,135 starved cycles.
The ARM helper reads the file in uniform 4,096-byte chunks, 3,699 reads for the whole file.

All 190 would-block events occur before the first byte is submitted; after the first read event the helper never blocks writing to the FPGA again. The FPGA-side input FIFO is therefore never full during steady delivery, which means the ARM-side file read throughput is the limiting factor and is consistent with the observed 1.38x realtime ceiling.
The 4,096-byte read granularity is a candidate cause of that ceiling and is the first concrete delivery-side mechanism identified.
open_conflicts: Block 1 capture 5 was warm and still gapped at 1.38x realtime, while all five block 2 runs at presumably equal or greater warmth are clean. Page-cache warmth alone therefore does not explain the difference, and core-reload freshness may be a second factor. The two cannot be separated with the data in hand.
scope_limitations: No genuine power-cycle sample has been taken since entry 568, and entry 568's own reboot predates the current syslog and cannot be verified.
The ARM helper log carries no timestamps, so it establishes read granularity and blocking behaviour but not read latency.
The archived helper log is from the final block 2 run only.
input_starved_cycles_since_previous_swap remains cumulative rather than contiguous.
Page-cache state is still not directly measured.
delivered_fps includes the startup hold in every run.
